title: Check if the Rectangle Corner Is Reachable
summary: Given two positive integers xCorner and yCorner, and a list of circles where each circle is defined by its center coordinates (xi, yi) and radius ri, determine if there exists a path from the bottom left corner of a rectangle (at the origin) to the top right corner (at coordinates (xCorner, yCorner)) such that the path lies entirely within the rectangle, does not touch or enter any circle, and touches the rectangle only at the two corners.
statement: Given two positive integers xCorner and yCorner, and a list of circles where each circle is defined by its center coordinates (xi, yi) and radius ri, determine if there exists a path from the bottom left corner of a rectangle (at the origin) to the top right corner (at coordinates (xCorner, yCorner)) such that the path lies entirely within the rectangle, does not touch or enter any circle, and touches the rectangle only at the two corners. Return true if such a path exists, and false otherwise.
constraints: x_corner and y_corner are at least three; circles contain positive center coordinates and radii.
A path must stay inside the rectangle from (0,0) to (x_corner,y_corner) without touching any circle.
Return false when a circle covers an endpoint or connected circle obstacles join left/top to right/bottom.
hints: A path is blocked exactly when obstacle components connect the rectangle’s left/top boundary to its right/bottom boundary.
Union intersecting circles and two virtual boundary nodes, while ignoring circle intersections occurring wholly beyond the relevant rectangle corner.
Reject covered endpoints; connect each circle to touched boundary sides and to qualifying intersecting circles.
Planar separation makes a left/top-to-right/bottom component necessary and sufficient for blocking opposite corners.
editorial: Planar separation makes a left/top-to-right/bottom component necessary and sufficient for blocking opposite corners.

tests.explanation: The circle does not form a boundary-to-boundary barrier, so a route remains.
The starting corner lies inside the circle, so no valid path exists.
